scenes.tts: Purified neurons fire, yet barely talk to each other. What are they missing?
scenes.visual: Title card: Astrocytes Build and Switch On. A dish of retinal ganglion cells with almost no glia; a sparse current trace.
scenes.narration: Purified neurons fire, yet barely talk to each other. What are they missing?

scenes.tts: Ben Barres's laboratory purified rat retinal ganglion cells, leaving cultures with almost no glia.
scenes.visual: Cells pass over antibody-coated dishes; only ganglion cells are kept. Label: immunopanning.
scenes.narration: Ben Barres's laboratory purified rat retinal ganglion cells, leaving cultures with almost no glia.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-seven, Frank Pfrieger and Barres reported that these neurons fired action potentials.
scenes.caption: In 1997, Frank Pfrieger and Barres reported that these neurons fired action potentials.
scenes.visual: Healthy neurons with action potential spikes. Credit: Pfrieger and Barres, 1997.
scenes.narration: In 1997, Frank Pfrieger and Barres reported that these neurons fired action potentials.

scenes.tts: But they showed little synaptic activity.
scenes.visual: The synaptic trace stays nearly flat.
scenes.narration: But they showed little synaptic activity.

scenes.tts: Astrocytes are not the only source. Neurons form some synapses without them.
scenes.visual: Scope card: astrocytes add to synapse formation; they are not its sole cause.
scenes.narration: Astrocytes are not the only source. Neurons form some synapses without them.

scenes.tts: The readout is the mini: the small current from one vesicle released on its own.
scenes.visual: A single small downward blip on a trace; label: one vesicle, one mini.
scenes.narration: The readout is the mini: the small current from one vesicle released on its own.

scenes.tts: Tetrodotoxin blocks action potentials. What remains depends on the synapses, not on how busy the neurons are.
scenes.visual: Spikes disappear from the trace; only small minis remain. Label: tetrodotoxin.
scenes.narration: Tetrodotoxin blocks action potentials. What remains depends on the synapses, not on how busy the neurons are.

scenes.tts: With firing blocked, mini frequency is roughly the number of synapses giving detectable minis, times their average release rate. Mini size reflects the receptors facing the vesicle, and the transmitter inside it.
scenes.visual: On screen: detected mini frequency ≈ synapses giving detectable minis × their average rate of release on its own. Mini size: receptors facing the vesicle, and transmitter in it.
scenes.narration: With firing blocked, mini frequency is roughly the number of synapses giving detectable minis, times their average release rate. Mini size reflects the receptors facing the vesicle, and the transmitter inside it.

scenes.tts: Now add a layer of glia that does not touch the neurons.
scenes.visual: A glial feeder layer lowered above the neurons, not touching them.
scenes.narration: Now add a layer of glia that does not touch the neurons.

scenes.tts: Mini frequency rose about twelvefold. Survival did not change.
scenes.visual: The mini trace fills with events. On screen: mini frequency about 12 times higher; survival unchanged.
scenes.narration: Mini frequency rose about twelvefold. Survival did not change.

scenes.tts: Predict. More synapses, or more release from each one?
scenes.visual: Prediction card: more synapses, or more release per synapse?
scenes.narration: Predict. More synapses, or more release from each one?

scenes.tts: Mini frequency alone cannot say. More minis can mean more synapses, more release, or synapses that start responding.
scenes.visual: The formula returns; both terms flash.
scenes.narration: Mini frequency alone cannot say. More minis can mean more synapses, more release, or synapses that start responding.

scenes.tts: So Pfrieger and Barres also counted synapses by electron microscopy. Glia raised the count only about two point three times.
scenes.caption: So Pfrieger and Barres also counted synapses by electron microscopy. Glia raised the count only about 2.3 times.
scenes.visual: Synapse counts from the same 1997 cultures: about 2.3 times more with glia. Credit: Pfrieger and Barres, 1997.
scenes.narration: So Pfrieger and Barres also counted synapses by electron microscopy. Glia raised the count only about 2.3 times.

scenes.tts: If the same share of synapses gave detectable minis, each would release about five times as often. So the paper read most of the rise as more effective synapses.
scenes.visual: On screen: 12 ÷ 2.3 ≈ 5 times more release per synapse, if the share of synapses giving detectable minis stayed the same. Note: minis also got larger, so some extra events may simply have become detectable.
scenes.narration: If the same share of synapses gave detectable minis, each would release about five times as often. So the paper read most of the rise as more effective synapses.

scenes.tts: In two thousand one, Erik Ullian and colleagues reported a sevenfold rise in synapses, in their own cultures. That is far more than the nineteen ninety-seven count, so how much is number and how much is efficacy depends on the culture.
scenes.caption: In 2001, Erik Ullian and colleagues reported a sevenfold rise in synapses, in their own cultures. That is far more than the 1997 count, so how much is number and how much is efficacy depends on the culture.
scenes.visual: A second, later study card: about 7 times more synapses with astrocytes, needed to keep them. Credit: Ullian and colleagues, 2001.
scenes.narration: In 2001, Erik Ullian and colleagues reported a sevenfold rise in synapses, in their own cultures. That is far more than the 1997 count, so how much is number and how much is efficacy depends on the culture.

scenes.tts: In two thousand five, Karen Christopherson and colleagues identified thrombospondins as astrocyte proteins that induce synapses.
scenes.caption: In 2005, Karen Christopherson and colleagues identified thrombospondins as astrocyte proteins that induce synapses.
scenes.visual: Astrocyte secreting thrombospondin; new synapses appear. Credit: Christopherson and colleagues, 2005.
scenes.narration: In 2005, Karen Christopherson and colleagues identified thrombospondins as astrocyte proteins that induce synapses.

scenes.tts: Those synapses looked normal by electron microscopy. They released transmitter. Yet they gave no AMPA receptor responses.
scenes.visual: Three lamps: There lit, Releases lit, Responds dark and labelled AMPA response near rest.
scenes.narration: Those synapses looked normal by electron microscopy. They released transmitter. Yet they gave no AMPA receptor responses.

scenes.tts: They were silent near rest. They lack working AMPA receptors, and any N M D A receptors there would be mostly blocked by magnesium.
scenes.caption: They were silent near rest. They lack working AMPA receptors, and any NMDA receptors there would be mostly blocked by magnesium.
scenes.visual: Label: silent synapse, no AMPA response near rest. Empty AMPA slot; a faded NMDA receptor marked 'if present, mostly blocked by magnesium'.
scenes.narration: They were silent near rest. They lack working AMPA receptors, and any NMDA receptors there would be mostly blocked by magnesium.

scenes.tts: They add to the count, but add no AMPA minis.
scenes.visual: The synapse count ticks up; the mini trace does not change.
scenes.narration: They add to the count, but add no AMPA minis.

scenes.tts: Later work found glypicans four and six, also from astrocytes. They recruit AMPA receptors, and the synapses respond.
scenes.caption: Later work found glypicans 4 and 6, also from astrocytes. They recruit AMPA receptors, and the synapses respond.
scenes.visual: AMPA receptors arrive at the silent synapses. Label: glypicans 4 and 6.
scenes.narration: Later work found glypicans 4 and 6, also from astrocytes. They recruit AMPA receptors, and the synapses respond.

scenes.tts: So astrocyte signals share the work. Thrombospondin mainly builds. The glypicans mainly switch synapses on.
scenes.visual: Two columns: thrombospondin, mainly builds; glypicans, mainly switch on. Small note: these assays do not show a fixed order.
scenes.narration: So astrocyte signals share the work. Thrombospondin mainly builds. The glypicans mainly switch synapses on.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: a synapse that is there is not yet a synapse that works. Count it, and record from it.
scenes.visual: Closing card: count it, and record from it. Small note: these assays do not show a fixed order of building and switching on.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: a synapse that is there is not yet a synapse that works. Count it, and record from it.
